newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin surgery may be delayed two months - surgeon.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin surgery may be delayed two months - surgeon.

text.p: A Russian surgeon chosen to carry out heart surgery on President Boris Yeltsin said on Sunday that the operation could be delayed by up to two months judging by the patient's condition.

Renat Akchurin said in an interview with NTV commercial television that Yeltsin, 65, would not accept the idea of cancelling the bypass surgery aimed at improving the blood supply to his heart because it would dramatically limit his physical activities.
Asked by Yevgeny Kiselyov, anchorman of the weekly show Itogi, when the operation might take place, Akchurin answered: "Within 1-1/2 or two months."

Asked whether the operation might be cancelled for good, Akchurin answered: "It is possible but special conditions should be created for the president then. We would be forced to limit his physical activies. He is not going to tolerate that."
Yeltsin said earlier this month that doctors had found problems with his heart and that he had agreed to an operation, likely to take place in late September.
Akchurin said a committee of Russian and foreign doctors was due to decide on Wednesday or Thursday when to conduct the operation and whether it was generally safe for the patient.
